learning_objective: 🎯 Learn about the crucial social and medical aspects of reproductive health, from population control methods to fighting STIs and exploring modern fertility treatments.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Rapid declines in death rates and maternal/infant mortality have caused huge population growth. Education and the use of contraceptives are heavily promoted to achieve smaller, healthier families.

Methods to prevent pregnancy. Includes Natural methods (timing), Barriers (condoms), IUDs (Copper-T inside the uterus), Oral pills (hormones that stop ovulation), and Surgical methods (Vasectomy in men, Tubectomy in women).
Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term (abortion). It is legalized in India under strict conditions to prevent misuse (like illegal female foeticide).
Diseases passed through sexual contact (HIV, Syphilis, Gonorrhoea, Genital Herpes). Most are completely curable if detected early, except for HIV, Hepatitis-B, and Genital Herpes.
Medical miracles for couples facing infertility. Includes IVF (In Vitro Fertilization - 'test-tube baby' where fertilization happens in a lab), ZIFT, GIFT, and Artificial Insemination.

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The Acronym Decoder
fun_activity.instructions: Reproductive health is full of acronyms! Challenge yourself to decode them: ART (Assisted Reproductive Technology), IUD (Intra Uterine Device), MTP (Medical Termination of Pregnancy), and IVF (In Vitro Fertilization).

exam_tips: 📌 Amniocentesis was designed to detect genetic disorders in the fetus, but it was banned for sex determination to stop female foeticide. Expect a question on its dual nature.
📌 Know the mechanism of action of IUDs: Copper T releases copper ions to suppress sperm motility, while hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation.
📌 Differentiate between Vasectomy (cutting the vas deferens in males) and Tubectomy (cutting the fallopian tubes in females).
quick_recap: ⭐ Barrier methods like condoms are the only contraceptives that also protect against STIs.
⭐ Oral contraceptive pills work primarily by inhibiting ovulation and altering cervical mucus to block sperm.
⭐ 'In vitro' means outside the body (in glass), while 'in vivo' means inside the living body.
